audits.title: EP.TU.370A 5-year re-audit of quality indicators for potentially curative rectal cancer resections by a single surgeon
audits.standard: Published standards for tumour perforation and CRM positivity
audits.setting: Craigavon Area Hospital, single surgeon's potentially curative rectal resections

cycle1.result: R0 resection 94.1%; R1 (nodes or deposit <1mm from margin) 3.92% and 1.96%; tumour perforation 3.92% (all pre-operative); local recurrence 5.88%; 90-day mortality 1.96%; median LOS 7 days.

audits.other_findings: This is a re-audit; the previous audit also showed rates below published standards but its figures are not given.
audits.citation: Lockhart J, McKay D. EP.TU.370A 5-year re-audit of quality indicators for potentially curative rectal cancer resections by a single surgeon. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab311.047.

audits.title: ThTP7.1 An audit of outcome of rectal cancer patients who were offered primary surgery. Are we following NICE guidelines for management of rectal cancer? –A retrospective cross sectional study at a District General Hospital
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on management of rectal cancer
audits.setting: Queens Hospital Burton on Trent, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Compliance with NICE guidelines not satisfactory (figures not reported); local recurrence 24%, distant metastasis 32%, disease free 52%, mortality 12% at median 34 months.

audits.other_findings: Outcomes were below those of national cancer centres of excellence.
audits.citation: Wani I, Husain N, Alam A, Narayanasamy S, Thomas P. ThTP7.1 An audit of outcome of rectal cancer patients who were offered primary surgery. Are we following NICE guidelines for management of rectal cancer? –A retrospective cross sectional study at a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.305.

audits.title: MRI directed multidisciplinary team preoperative treatment strategy: the way to eliminate positive circumferential margins?
audits.setting: Rectal cancer treatment network (Royal Marsden Hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall CRM+ve rate 12.5% (32/256) in nonpalliative patients; 26% (16/62) with surgery alone without MRI-based MDT discussion vs 1% (1/116) with MDT discussion

audits.intervention: Policy of mandatory preoperative MRI-based MDT discussion

cycle2.result: Overall CRM+ve rate 7% (5/70); surgery-alone CRM+ve rate 3% (1/37)

audits.other_findings: 39 (13%) of patients were palliative; 178 had surgery alone and 81 neoadjuvant therapy in the first cycle.
audits.citation: Burton S, Brown G, Daniels IR, Norman AR, Mason B, Cunningham D, et al.. MRI directed multidisciplinary team preoperative treatment strategy: the way to eliminate positive circumferential margins?. Br J Cancer. 2006;94(3):351-357. doi:10.1038/sj.bjc.6602947. PMID: 16465171.

audits.title: Variability in the quality of rectal cancer care in public hospitals in Catalonia (Spain): clinical audit as a basis for action.

cycle1.result: TME reported by surgeons in 46.4% and pathologists in 36.2%; preoperative radiotherapy in 52% of stage II and III patients.

audits.other_findings: Low-caseload hospitals had more Hartmann's procedures, worse TME quality and more complications; care was reorganised.
audits.citation: Manchon-Walsh P, Borras JM, Espinas JA, Aliste L, Catalonian Rectal Cancer Group. Variability in the quality of rectal cancer care in public hospitals in Catalonia (Spain): clinical audit as a basis for action. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2011;37(4):325-333. doi:10.1016/j.ejso.2011.01.014. PMID: 21296543.

audits.title: Improving quality of care and clinical outcomes for rectal cancer through clinical audits in a multicentre cancer care organisation.
audits.standard: Quality indicators for neoadjuvant radiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer
audits.intervention: Quality improvement action plan designed from the baseline audit (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: MRI re-staging 61.5%; unreported ypCRM 5.6% (p value truncated).

audits.other_findings: Standardised MRI staging reports in 77.5%; only 9.7% of interrupted treatments received a compensation dose; overall treatment time still needs work.
audits.citation: Torras MG, Canals E, Muñoz-Montplet C, Vidal A, Jurado D, Eraso A, et al.. Improving quality of care and clinical outcomes for rectal cancer through clinical audits in a multicentre cancer care organisation. Radiat Oncol. 2020;15(1):28. doi:10.1186/s13014-020-1465-z. PMID: 32005123.
